test_title: PYST 68: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:

He had a strong **will** to overcome adversity.

options.text: They signed a will before retirement.
The king ruled with willful pride.
She was willing to help without reward.

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The word **"will"** in the context of the highlighted sentence refers to a strong determination to achieve something or overcome a challenge. (इच्छाशक्ति) • **Example: **He had the will to persevere through difficult times. • The word **"will"** in Option 1 refers to a legal document that states how a person's property will be distributed after their death. (वसीयत) • **Example: **Before his passing, he made sure to prepare a will to divide his assets among his children. • Both uses of the word "will" are homonyms, as they are spelled the same but have different meanings. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: The king ruled with willful pride** (हठी स्वाभिमान के साथ राजा ने शासन किया) – The word "willful" means showing a stubborn and determined intention to do as one wants, regardless of the consequences. • **Example: **Her willful nature often caused conflicts with her peers. • **Option 3: She was willing to help without reward** (वह बिना इनाम के मदद करने को तैयार थी) – The word "willing" means ready, eager, or prepared to do something. • **Example: **He was willing to take on additional responsibilities at work. • **Option 4: The team showed great willpower** (टीम ने महान इच्छाशक्ति दिखाई) – The word "willpower" refers to the ability to control one's actions, emotions, or urges. • **Example: **It takes a lot of willpower to resist eating dessert every day. 5e:Tb3d, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "The chef pan-seared a salmon fillet with herbs."
